thread.title: Apple Pay transaction volume tripled in Q2 (AAPL)

author: Rachel Green
title: Apple Pay transaction volume tripled in Q2 (AAPL)
text:
This story was delivered to Business Insider Intelligence " Payments Briefing " subscribers hours before appearing on Business Insider. To be the first to know, please click here .
Apple Pay surpassed 1 billion transactions in Apple's fiscal Q3 2018 (ended June 30, 2018), indicating that its transaction volume tripled annually, as highlighted in the firm's earnings presentation , held on July 31. For context, the firm's transaction volume grew 200% annually.
Business Insider Intelligence
While the 1 billion milestone is a notable feat — Apple Pay launched at the end of 2014 — the firm does not provide further context as to what drove that growth, making it hard to assess how the wallet's performance is stacking up. Apple Pay is well positioned relative to other services.In the firm's earnings call, Apple CEO Tim Cook pointed out that Apple Pay completed more mobile transactions than some of its competitors, including Square and PayPal, though these firms don't provide that data in full themselves.
It's worth noting, though, that while Apple Pay does offer buy buttons for Safari and a new peer-to-peer (P2P) payments offering, PayPal's nonmobile and nonstore services are much more developed than Apple Pay's, giving it a leg up.
The firm announced two growth initiatives that could accelerate and sustain growth. First, Apple will continue to expand Apple Pay internationally. Apple Pay plans to launch in Germany, which will be its twenty-fifth global market, later this year. Although it's hard to assess how Apple Pay's performance is stacking up due to the lack of context provided, it's likely that much of the wallet's growth can be attributed to new audiences that it obtains from launching internationally.
And Germany represents an especially good opportunity since it has a long runway for digital payments growth, with cash still comprising 74% of total transactions, making the German market ripe for digital payments innovation. Although only approximately 27% of the German population uses iOS devices, Apple Pay could still see high usage in the country because it's the only NFC mobile wallet option for iPhone users, so there's likely pent-up demand for the wallet.
It seems that international growth has been Apple's main strategy to scale Apple Pay, and identifying more key markets where it can gain a footing early into the region's digital payment development will likely allow Apple Pay to see strong uptake.
Second, Apple will focus on bolstering its US accessibility. eBay has already started enabling its sellers to accept Apple Pay online. Meanwhile, CVS Pharmacy and 7-Eleven, which have over 9,000 and 7,890 US locations respectively, will start accepting Apple Pay at all of their US locations this fall.
Apple Pay can use those partnerships to do better in its primary market, where it's been struggling; adoption in the US has stagnated at about 25% of eligible users, and it's growing much slower than international markets as Apple Pay expands abroad.
These initiatives can help bolster Apple Pay's position in the US, as expanding its acceptance network is imperative to encouraging repeat usage. And becoming a payment option at convenience stores and pharmacies, where consumers typically go for repeat purchases, can encourage habit formation, which can ultimately drive the mobile wallet's volume.
